segments.text: X five is the Nine-Point Center: the center of the remarkable circle of radius R over two that passes through nine classical points of triangle A B C— the three side midpoints M sub a, M sub b, M sub c, the three altitude feet H sub a, H sub b, H sub c, and the three Euler midpoints toward the orthocenter.

segments.text: Its trilinear coordinates are cosine of B minus C, to cosine of C minus A, to cosine of A minus B. On the central lines layer, X five is the exact midpoint between Circumcenter X three and Orthocenter X four on the Euler line, and joins Incenter X one on the Feuerbach line through X eleven.

segments.text: Under functional relations, X five is the complement of the Circumcenter X three, the isogonal conjugate of the Kosnita point X fifty-four, and the isotomic conjugate of X ninety-five. Across all four reference triangles, the nine-point circle centered at X five remains tangent to the incircle at the Feuerbach point X eleven.
